newsitem.title: FINLAND: AAMULEHTI SEES NO MERGER APPROVAL PROBLEM.
newsitem.headline: AAMULEHTI SEES NO MERGER APPROVAL PROBLEM.

text.p: Finnish media group Aamulehti said on Tuesday it did not foresee any problems with approval from authorities of its planned merger with commercial television channel MTV Oy announced earlier.
The deal was subject to approval and concessions from the authorities, Aamulehti and MTV said in a statement.
"I think they will welcome that ownership (of MTV) will be spread ... and at the moment we can foresee now problems with approvals," Aamulehti CEO Matti Packalen told a news conference.

Shares in MTV -- except Aamulehti's 20.3 percent stake -- will each give 137.5 shares in the new group to be formed and listed at the start of next year, and Aamulehti's shares will give one share each.
The group will have some 3,000 owners and Swedish Marieberg will be its biggest owner, targetting a 20 percent stake, Packalen said.
To avoid making the merger complicated, the new group will have two share series, as Aamulehti has, Packalen said. The series I stock will have 10 times more votes than the series II stock.
